messages.content: It's extremely hot today and my air conditioner is currently turned off. Set it to start cooling at 20 degrees Celsius mid wind strength. power off after an hour

function.name: ThinQ_Connect
function.description: Sends a command to control an appliance, allowing only a single value to be sent in one call. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

body.description: A dictionary containing the parameters for the appliance command.

airConJobMode.description: The current job mode of the air conditioner.

windStrength.description: The strength of the air flow.

monitoringEnabled.description: Whether air quality sensor monitoring is enabled.

airCleanOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air cleaning function.

airConOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air conditioner, indicating if it is turned on or off.

powerSaveEnabled.description: Whether power save mode is enabled to conserve energy.

targetTemperature.description: The target temperature to set for the appliance, in degrees Celsius.

relativeHourToStop.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeMinuteToStop.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeHourToStart.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

relativeMinuteToStart.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

message.reasoning:
We need to parse user request: "Set it to start cooling at 20 degrees Celsius mid wind strength. power off after an hour." They want to turn on AC with cooling mode, target temp 20°C, wind strength mid, schedule to power off after an hour. Also they mention "mid wind strength". So we need to send command with airConJobMode: "COOL", targetTemperature: 20, windStrength: "MID", airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON" (to start). Then schedule to power off after an hour: relativeHourToStop: 1, relativeMinuteToStop: 0. Also relativeHourToStart and relativeMinuteToStart? Since they want to start now? They didn't specify start time; maybe start immediately. But we can set relativeHourToStart: 0, relativeMinuteToStart: 0? Or leave as null? The function expects values; but we can set relativeHourToStart: 0, relativeMinuteToStart: 0 to start immediately. However the function may interpret null as no scheduling. We might set relativeHourToStart: 0, relativeMinuteToStart: 0. Let's check the function signature: relativeHourToStart?: number, relativeMinuteToStart?: number. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start. So we can set them to 0 to start immediately. But maybe it's better to set them to null because we want immediate start. But we also want to start now. Setting them to null means no scheduling; but we still set airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON" which starts now. So we don't need to schedule start. So we can set relativeHourToStart: null, relativeMinuteToStart: null. For stop: relativeHourToStop: 1, relativeMinuteToStop: 0.

Also we need to set airConJobMode: "COOL", windStrength: "MID", targetTemperature: 20, airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON".

Also we might set other fields to defaults: monitoringEnabled: false, airCleanOperationMode: "STOP", powerSaveEnabled: false.

Thus we call ThinQ_Connect with body:

{
airConJobMode: "COOL",
windStrength: "MID",
targetTemperature: 20,
airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON",
relativeHourToStop: 1,
relativeMinuteToStop: 0,
relativeHourToStart: null,
relativeMinuteToStart: null
}

But we need to include all optional keys? Not necessary. We'll just provide those needed.

Let's produce JSON accordingly.
